$comment: Shared transport fixture. W4 Transport replaces per-language ad hoc HTTP calls with one injectable seam, and these cases pin the normalized request and response shape so a call recorded against one SDK replays identically through another. Go, TypeScript, and PHP already have a seam; Python calls urllib.request.urlopen directly and Rust takes a concrete reqwest::blocking::Client, which is why transport.injection is divergent in ops/build/sdk-paradigm.json.

request.header_canonicalization: Header names are matched case-insensitively and serialized in a stable order so two SDKs produce byte-comparable requests.
required_rules: A credential endpoint request carries Cache-Control: no-store, matching the server's own no-store response policy.
No secret value ever appears in a URL, a redirect, or an error message.
Form bodies are application/x-www-form-urlencoded with deterministic key ordering.
JSON bodies are UTF-8 with no trailing newline.

cases.why: The most security-sensitive request the SDK makes: it carries a code_verifier, which must never be logged or placed in a URL.
Rotation-sensitive: the response refresh token replaces the old one, and a refresh never carries a verifier.
HTTP Basic takes precedence over body credentials, so a client secret belongs in the Authorization header and never in the form body.
Carries a bearer and a product selector; the commercial projection must be read through the injected transport like any other call.
Carries a one-time license key or invitation code in a JSON body; the credential is never retained in login state or the state store.
The canonical resource-server call; the transport forwards the bearer unchanged and never logs it.

invariants: A transport double replays these cases byte-identically in every language.
Redirect construction is a pure function of its inputs and performs no I/O, so it is testable without a transport.
No transport implementation is allowed to log a header whose name matches Authorization, DPoP, or a credential form field.
Timeout and retry policy live in the transport, not in the session layer, so both are substitutable in one place.
